newsitem.title: HAITI: Tires burned in protest of Haitian police brutality.
newsitem.headline: Tires burned in protest of Haitian police brutality.

text.p: Demonstrators blocked roads and burned tires in Haiti's capital on Monday to protest the way police broke up last week's anti-government march in which one man's hand was blown off by a tear gas cannister.

"The police can blow off our hands but we'll still fight with our fists," said a protester who called himself "Never Innocent," standing by a burning car and tires blocking a road in the slum of Cite Soleil just outside the capital.

Some of the poorest Haitians said they had lost hope under the current government, which had not dealt with unemployment that ranged as high as 80 percent and extreme poverty in which the average Haitian lived on $250 a year.

At Friday's demonstration, some 60 organisations called for Prime Minister Rosny Smarth to step down. Demonstrators and parliamentarians have called him incompetent and criticised a government plan to privatise nine key state-run businesses including the telephone and electricity companies.
Crowd control police dispersed the small crowd by throwing explosive tear gas cannisters. Dieusel Sibil, a 23-year-old unemployed man, lost his hand when he tried to pick up one of the cannisters.
The police action was condemned by human rights groups and the U.N. civilian mission in Haiti.

Smarth went to parliament Monday to defend the actions of police. He tried to assure lawmakers that the Haitian government has focused on ways to create jobs and improve Haiti's economy. "In our first 10 months, we have been trying to form an economic base for Haiti," he said.
Smarth was appointed by president Rene Preval in March.
Parliamentarians welcomed Smarth's visit, calling it a rare event for a prime minister, but said they were unimpressed. "There is a lot of talk, and no action," said Senator Firmin Jean-Louis.
Police Chief Pierre Denize made no apologies for the police action last week, although he did express sympathy for the man who lost his hands in the incident on Friday.
A flier calling for a general strike circulated in the capital on Monday warning people to stay in their homes, close businesses and keep their children out of school on Thursday.
"Not even a rat has the right to be on the street," said the flier, claiming support of more than 160 organisations.

U.S. Ambassador William Lacey Swing continued to support Smarth and his initiatives to privatise. "There is bipartisan support in the United States for Haiti to modernise its economy," Swing said in a statement that also said he was impressed with Smarth's efforts in the past year.

World Bank, Inter-American Development Bank and European Community officials arrived in Port-au-Prince on Monday for a two-week visit to evaluate the economic situation in the Caribbean country and negotiate future aid.
